evidence_boundary.required_next_step: Add a controlled debug-only normal-mode and fault-trigger test hook, or use a separately qualified dedicated fault-injection firmware, before claiming bus-off/manual fault-injection coverage.
evidence_boundary.statement: The current P3B qualification firmware and host tools can observe MCAN error state but cannot safely initiate the normal-mode transmit behavior required for a controlled bus-off/manual fault-injection test.

findings.assertion: The qualification controller is configured listen-only with TX buffers disabled and TX disarmed.
Every product-firmware TX submission is rejected as disarmed.
The USB owner forwards pending TX requests into the permanently disarmed MCAN owner path.
The HIL collector rejects devices that are not listen-only, TX-disarmed, and without automatic recovery attempts.
The protocol smoke tool also requires listen-only and TX-disarmed state.
Firmware diagnostics observe PSR/ECR bus state and explicitly perform no automatic bus-off recovery.
The generic build-time fault injection covers RTOS assert, stack-overflow, and allocation failures, not MCAN faults.
The generic build-time fault selector exposes only the three RTOS fault modes.
A separate Phase 0 probe can enter normal mode for bounded TX, but it is not the P3B qualification firmware or product host path.
